mainEntity.name: What does a holistic doctor actually do?

acceptedAnswer.text: A holistic doctor looks at your whole body and life rather than one symptom in isolation. I use functional medicine to map how your hormones, gut, metabolism, stress, and nutrition connect, run advanced labs, and build a personalized plan to treat the root cause.

Yes. I hold a Ph.D. in Functional Medicine and am board certified in holistic health. Care here is grounded in advanced lab testing and physiology, read against optimal ranges, not guesswork or generic wellness advice.

mainEntity.name: How is a holistic doctor different from my regular doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your regular doctor often has fifteen minutes and one symptom to address. As a holistic doctor in Atlanta, I take the time to look at the whole system, connect the dots between your symptoms, and treat what is actually driving them.

mainEntity.name: What conditions can a holistic doctor help with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hormones, PCOS, gut and digestion, chronic fatigue, hair loss, menopause, weight, and more. Anything where the root cause sits across several systems is exactly where whole-person care helps most.

mainEntity.name: Do you work alongside my regular doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Functional medicine care here is provided alongside, not in place of, your primary and specialty care. We coordinate so the whole picture stays connected.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer virtual visits or only in person in Atlanta?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. See me in person at our Atlanta clinic, or virtually anywhere in Georgia. Your $99 Symptom Consultation can be booked either way.

sections.label: Hero

headings.text: A holistic doctor in Atlanta who treats the whole you.

paragraphs: If you have spent years feeling rushed, brushed off, or told your labs are normal while you still feel unwell, you deserve a doctor who looks closer and listens longer.

I am Dr. Nina Ross, ND PhD. I practice root-cause functional medicine here in Atlanta and virtually across Georgia. That means I read your whole story, your hormones, your gut, your metabolism, the stress you carry, until I find what is really driving how you feel. Then I build the plan around your body and your life, with you in the room the whole way.

imageSlots.alt: Dr. Nina Ross, a holistic doctor in Atlanta, with a patient at her functional medicine clinic

sections.label: If this sounds familiar

headings.text: You have been to doctors. You still do not feel heard.

paragraphs: You are not difficult, and you are not imagining it. You have just never been given the time.

sections.label: Meet Dr. Nina

headings.text: The doctor who looks closer and listens longer.

paragraphs: For years I watched people, so many of them women who looked like me, carry symptoms that no one would slow down to explain. So I built the practice I wished they could walk into. One where you are believed first, investigated thoroughly, and treated as a whole person with a life, not a fifteen minute slot.
When someone finally feels seen, the healing has already begun.

sections.label: Why whole-person care

headings.text: One doctor who finally connects every part of your health.

paragraphs: Most care is split into fifteen-minute visits, one symptom at a time, with no one looking at how it all fits together. A holistic doctor holds the whole picture, your hormones, gut, metabolism, sleep, and stress, and treats them as the connected system they really are.
You should never have to convince your doctor that you know your own body.

imageSlots.alt: Dr. Nina Ross, a holistic doctor in Atlanta, sitting with a patient

boldPairs.title: One connected picture
boldPairs.body: Your symptoms are read together, not in separate silos, so the thread linking them finally shows.

boldPairs.title: Time to be heard
boldPairs.body: An unhurried first visit means nothing about how you feel gets rushed past or dismissed.

boldPairs.title: Care that fits your life
boldPairs.body: Your plan honors how you actually eat, move, and live, not a template made for someone else.

sections.label: What holistic means

headings.text: Holistic does not mean unscientific. It means whole.

paragraphs: Holistic has been worn down into a spa word. Here it carries its real weight. I treat the whole person with rigorous, lab-driven medicine, reading how every system in your body talks to the others, then following that conversation to the root.
This is medicine that respects both your science and your story.

imageSlots.alt: Advanced functional medicine lab work at Dr. Nina Ross's Atlanta clinic

boldPairs.title: Real labs, read for optimal
boldPairs.body: Advanced panels read against where you actually feel well, not just inside a wide normal range.

boldPairs.title: The whole system, connected
boldPairs.body: Hormones, gut, metabolism, and stress are mapped together so the real driver cannot hide.

boldPairs.title: A plan you help build
boldPairs.body: Care shaped around your body and your real life, with you in the room deciding.
